newsitem.title: USA: Md. says Q1 revenues, job growth show expansion.
newsitem.headline: Md. says Q1 revenues, job growth show expansion.

text.p: Maryland's economic growth for the first three months of 1997 has kept pace with the national expansion, with tax revenues and job growth outpacing 1996 levels, the state comptroller said.
Sales and use tax receipts generated $465.3 million, 7.3 percent more than in the same period last year, Comptroller Louis Goldstein said in a statement.
Employment grew by 2.5 percent for the first quarter, compared with national employment growth of 2.3 percent.
"Growth in the last quarter of 1996 was 6.6 percent over the same period of the previous year, producing sales tax receipts of $570.7 million," Goldstein said.
The Comptroller said the figures show "Maryland's economic growth isn't a one-time blip on the chart but a continuing trend."
